source.title: City of Bastrop FY2025-26 Annual Operating & Capital Budget

meta.note: The City of Bastrop (the county seat) — a separate government from Bastrop County. The bars are the city's General Fund ($18.6M). Police is the largest single department at about a third of it; Police and Fire together are about 43%. Each amount links to the exact page of the adopted budget where it appears. Bastrop also runs its own electric utility (Bastrop Power & Light, $9.5M) and a Water & Wastewater fund ($10.0M) as self-supporting enterprises. One honest note on the arithmetic: the department pages sum to a little less than the $18.6M General-Fund total, because the city books some fund-wide costs (internal-service charges, and a non-departmental overhead-allocation credit) outside the individual departments. That remainder is shown as its own line so the tree still adds up to the dollar; the city's by-category view of the same fund (wages, benefits, supplies, and so on, pp. 41-44) foots to $18,608,924 exactly.
facts: Police is the largest General-Fund department — $6.23M, about a third of the fund.
Police and Fire together are about 43% of the General Fund (not two-thirds — Fire is $1.79M).
The city cut its FY2026 property-tax rate to $0.5040 per $100, down from a proposed $0.5179.
Bastrop owns its electric utility — Bastrop Power & Light — a $9.5M enterprise fund.
This is the CITY of Bastrop, distinct from Bastrop County ($93.7M).
